title: Psychology of Prophetism: A Secular Look at the Bible
lede: Elst, raised Catholic in Flanders, introduces Indian readers to Dr. Herman Somers, a former Jesuit from Antwerp with doctorates in philosophy, classics, theology and psychology. Somers reads the Bible as a record of real people and asks what state of mind the experiences it describes imply. His answer is that many prophets heard voices, and that Jesus fits the profile of “paraphrenia”: a rare condition with a lasting delusion about one's parentage, fed by occasional hallucinations. Elst ends by warning Hindus against picturing the prophets as yogis.

note: This book offers a psychiatric explanation of religious figures whom believers hold sacred, and its conclusions are rejected by Christian scholarship. Diagnosing historical figures from texts is speculative. This page reports Somers's and Elst's claims as theirs, in neutral terms.

sections.lede: Somers starts by assuming the texts preserve real experiences, then asks what psychology fits them. Elst stresses that not every prophet is “diagnosed”: some were shrewd, some fanatical, some clairvoyant.
